## Purpose

The vocabulary of the business, expressed as types that make illegal states unrepresentable. Money, Currency, Price, Quantity, Lot, Symbol, and the arithmetic over them. This is the most important module in the system: every financial error downstream is either an error here or an error that this module failed to make impossible.

## What gets built

- fixed-point decimal representation with explicit scale per currency
- checked arithmetic: no silent overflow, no silent truncation
- currency-tagged Money that refuses cross-currency arithmetic
- explicit, named rounding policies applied at documented boundaries
- serialization that is exact and round-trip stable

## Invariants

These are executed as tests at gate **G4**. A module may not declare an
invariant it does not test.

- INV-001: Money arithmetic never uses IEEE-754 floating point.
- INV-002: a + b == b + a for Money of the same currency.
- INV-003: (a + b) - b == a exactly, under the declared rounding policy.
- INV-004: Money of different currencies cannot be added; it is a compile-time error.
- INV-005: every rounding operation names its policy and its scale.

## Test obligations

- property: commutativity, associativity, identity, inverse
- property: round-trip serialization is exact
- boundary: min/max representable, zero, negative, scale limits
- fuzz: arbitrary operation sequences never panic and never overflow silently

## Known failure modes

The things that go wrong in systems like this one. Each should map to a test above.

- float creeps in through a third-party library or a JSON boundary
- rounding applied twice, or applied at an undocumented boundary
